correctness.rationale: Projecting onto constants, zero-sum partwise constants and the within-part differences gives eigenvalues 0, N and N−s, respectively. The diagonal and cross-part signs are immediate; a pair within a part of fraction p has sign given by F_p(x)−kappa with x=N(1+N eta)t. The integrand g_p increases strictly from 0 to 1/p, so its running average crosses each kappa in (0,1) exactly once; it decreases strictly with p, making the largest part decisive. At t=0 the matrix is the identity. In x coordinates the optimized quantity NT has derivative 1−g_p(x); its one zero, x*=log((2−p)/(1−p)), lies in range since the running average is less than g_p(x*)=1. Substituting p+(1−p)e^(−x*)=1/(2−p) gives the stated value. Strict ordering persists after maximization by evaluating at the attained optimizer for the smaller p. The one-deleted-edge graph is one minimizer, not the only one: all noncomplete graphs with largest part two tie. The star is the unique maximizing shape up to isomorphism. The expansion g_p(x)=x+O(x²) and continuity at the inverse level 1 give the coupling limits; taking p→0 and p→1 verifies the shape ratio. Complete graphs stay nonnegative. The nested checker was inspected, not executed; the recorded numerical checks are corroboration only.
residual_risks: Claims are for the unweighted counting-measure Laplacian; the proof does not transfer directly to normalized or conductance-weighted graphs.
The finite matrix checker is not a proof of the continuum statement.

value.rationale: The exact global sign boundary and unique worst strength answer a natural question not settled by eventual positivity. The reduction shows that the largest part alone governs the delay even among highly unequal shapes, resolves all extremal ties, and gives a quantitative limiting comparison of optimized delays.
residual_risks: Value is claimed for this natural graph family, not for arbitrary networks or numerical integrators.
